subject: Creativity
title: Internet Comedy: Memes as the New Folk Humor
description: A 60-second lesson on Internet Comedy: Memes as the New Folk Humor.

hook.text: A meme format survives about 4 months before dying. Medieval jesters lasted decades.

buildup.text: Internet memes are the first truly democratic comedy form — created by millions, filtered by crowds, spread by shares.

discovery.text: Memes function like folk jokes of the past — anonymous, iterative, remixed endlessly.

twist.text: Most meme creators are never credited. Like medieval joke-tellers, they create for the community, not for fame.

climax.text: TikTok compressed comedy to 60 seconds. Twitter compressed jokes to 280 characters. Vine (RIP) did it in 6 seconds.

punchline.text: The internet didn't kill comedy. It just gave everyone a microphone and 6.

quiz.question: How are internet memes similar to medieval folk jokes?
options: Both are anonymous, iterative, and remixed by communities

details.summary: Internet memes function as modern folk humor, created and shared by communities rather than professional comedians. Memes evolve through iteration as users remix templates, creating a collaborative comedy form that spreads at unprecedented speed.
details.whyItMatters: Memes democratized comedy creation by removing the need for professional skills or platforms. They represent the biggest shift in how humor is produced and consumed since television replaced vaudeville.
takeaways: Memes are collaborative comedy created by communities
They spread and evolve through remix and iteration
Internet humor moves faster than any previous comedy format

faq.question: Why are memes compared to folk humor?
faq.answer: Like folk tales and jokes, memes are created anonymously, modified by communities, and spread through sharing rather than professional distribution. No single author owns a meme format, just as no one owns a folk joke.

faq.question: Can memes be considered real comedy?
faq.answer: Yes. Memes use the same principles as traditional comedy including incongruity, timing, and cultural reference. Their format is different, but the underlying humor mechanics are identical to any other comedy form.
